name: Complicit or infiltrated financial institutions and insiders
description: Criminals gain access to the financial system by corrupting or recruiting staff, acquiring control of an institution, or using a counterparty institution whose own controls are weak or deliberately bypassed. Defensive focus is on spotting the signs at three levels: the individual insider, the institution's own governance and reporting, and counterparty institutions whose behaviour no longer matches their size and customer base.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services, 2016
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Sound management of risks related to money laundering and financing of terrorism, 2014 (revised 2020)

exposure.rationale: Insider and counterparty-bank complicity; correspondent/respondent relationships and staff override.

indicators.name: Staff override of controls or excessive record access
indicators.canon: Staff override of controls or excessive record access
indicators.desc: Employees override approvals, alter records, access records without need or show unusual relationships with customers.
indicators.ctx: Staff bypass or override screening, monitoring or approval steps, or access records of customers outside their duties, for a particular set of customers.
indicators.fp: Privileged roles and emergency fixes legitimately involve overrides; require documented approval.

indicators.name: Insider override of credit policy or unusual speed of approval
indicators.canon: Insider override of credit policy or unusual speed of approval
indicators.desc: Staff-approved exceptions or rapid decisions with limited verification.
indicators.ctx: Credit, onboarding or exception approvals are pushed through unusually fast by the same employee, with thin verification, for connected customers.
indicators.fp: May have innocent explanations; assess in context of customer profile and other indicators.

indicators.name: Employee accounts receive unusual payments
indicators.desc: Staff accounts credited from customers, vendors or dormant accounts.
indicators.ctx: Employee or relative accounts receive payments from customers or vendors, a sign of bribes or commissions for favourable treatment.

indicators.name: Screening alerts closed repeatedly for the same pattern with minimal rationale
indicators.canon: Screening alerts closed repeatedly for the same pattern with minimal rationale
indicators.desc: Internal indicator of weak alert handling that may mask manipulation.
indicators.ctx: Alerts on the same customers or pattern are closed repeatedly with minimal rationale, which may reflect an insider shielding activity.

indicators.name: Respondent serves undisclosed downstream institutions
indicators.desc: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.
indicators.ctx: A correspondent or respondent institution is found to be offering access to undisclosed downstream banks or payment firms.
indicators.fp: Group and agency arrangements are disclosed normally.

indicators.name: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
indicators.canon: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
indicators.desc: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.
indicators.ctx: A counterparty bank's flows are far beyond what its balance sheet and customer base can explain, suggesting it is being used as a conduit.

indicators.name: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
indicators.canon: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
indicators.desc: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.
indicators.ctx: A counterparty institution is found to deal with shell banks or unlicensed entities, or to be controlled by one.

indicators.name: Institution ownership or control passes to opaque parties followed by a volume surge
indicators.canon: Institution ownership or control passes to opaque parties followed by a volume surge
indicators.desc: A bank, payment firm or other regulated entity changes owners, directors or key managers to parties whose backing is unclear, and soon afterwards shows sharply higher volumes, new customer types or new corridors.
indicators.ctx: Marks the point at which a previously sound institution may have been taken over to serve criminal flows.
indicators.fp: Genuine acquisitions, recapitalisations and expansion strategies change ownership and volumes together. Verify the new owners' source of wealth and business plan.

indicators.name: Internal reporting on specific customers blocked, withdrawn or never raised
indicators.canon: Internal reporting on specific customers blocked, withdrawn or never raised
indicators.desc: Staff or managers discourage unusual-activity reports on a customer, reverse escalations, or reports for a particular relationship repeatedly fail to arrive at the compliance function.
indicators.ctx: Core complicity sign, as the human reporting chain is the control being neutralised.
indicators.fp: Reports may be legitimately closed after review or consolidated into one case. Look for patterns tied to one manager or portfolio.

indicators.name: Manual entries through internal or suspense accounts hiding customer flows
indicators.canon: Manual entries through internal or suspense accounts hiding customer flows
indicators.desc: Funds move via manual journals, suspense, clearing or staff-controlled internal accounts, so customer-level records do not show the real origin, destination or beneficial party.
indicators.ctx: Lets an insider move or conceal funds outside normal monitoring, and is usually found by audit or ledger analytics.
indicators.fp: Operational corrections, reconciliations and settlement timing legitimately use internal accounts. Review ageing, authorisers and counterparties.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
